---------------------------- MODULE W4Od6m5p5t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Controllers, Proposals, Quorum

VARIABLES
    proposed,      \* proposals that have been raised
    inflight,      \* set of <<controller, proposal>> votes cast but not yet delivered
    votes,         \* proposal -> set of controllers whose votes were delivered
    decided,       \* proposals for which a quorum has been observed
    motionLog,     \* append-only sequence of proposals physically dispatched
    beacon         \* status lamp that keeps toggling while the bank is powered

vars == <<proposed, inflight, votes, decided, motionLog, beacon>>

LoggedProposals == { motionLog[i] : i \in 1..Len(motionLog) }

TypeOK ==
    /\ proposed \subseteq Proposals
    /\ inflight \subseteq (Controllers \X Proposals)
    /\ votes \in [Proposals -> SUBSET Controllers]
    /\ decided \subseteq Proposals
    /\ motionLog \in Seq(Proposals)
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ proposed = {}
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ votes = [p \in Proposals |-> {}]
    /\ decided = {}
    /\ motionLog = << >>
    /\ beacon = FALSE

Raise(p) ==
    /\ p \notin proposed
    /\ proposed' = proposed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, votes, decided, motionLog, beacon>>

CastVote(c, p) ==
    /\ p \in proposed
    /\ c \notin votes[p]
    /\ <<c, p>> \notin inflight
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {<<c, p>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, votes, decided, motionLog, beacon>>

\* Reordering: any in-flight vote may be delivered in any order.
DeliverVote(c, p) ==
    /\ <<c, p>> \in inflight
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {<<c, p>>}
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, decided, motionLog, beacon>>

MarkDecided(p) ==
    /\ Cardinality(votes[p]) >= Quorum
    /\ p \notin decided
    /\ decided' = decided \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, inflight, votes, motionLog, beacon>>

Dispatch(p) ==
    /\ p \in decided
    /\ p \notin LoggedProposals
    /\ motionLog' = Append(motionLog, p)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, inflight, votes, decided, beacon>>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposed, inflight, votes, decided, motionLog>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Proposals : Raise(p)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, p \in Proposals : CastVote(c, p)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers, p \in Proposals : DeliverVote(c, p)
    \/ \E p \in Proposals : MarkDecided(p)
    \/ \E p \in Proposals : Dispatch(p)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Each irreversible dispatch happens at most once: no proposal is logged twice.
DispatchAtMostOnce ==
    \A i, j \in 1..Len(motionLog) : (i # j) => (motionLog[i] # motionLog[j])

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    Proposals = {p1, p2}
    Quorum = 2

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT DispatchAtMostOnce
nl:
A skyscraper elevator bank is controlled by a small set of dispatch controllers that must agree before a car is physically sent to a floor. Any controller may raise a dispatch proposal for a waiting call. Controllers then cast approval votes for a proposal, but these votes travel over an internal bus that can reorder them arbitrarily, so a vote cast late may be delivered before one cast early. A proposal is considered decided only once a quorum of distinct controllers has had its votes delivered for it. Once a proposal is decided, the controller hardware actually dispatches the car, which is a physical, irreversible motion that cannot be recalled. Because votes can be reordered and redelivered, the danger is that the same proposal is acted on twice and a car is commanded to move for an already-served call. The system records each physical dispatch as an entry in an append-only motion log.
SAFETY PROPERTY: No proposal ever appears more than once in the physical dispatch motion log, so each irreversible car dispatch happens at most once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od5m1p6t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Players, MaxEpoch, NONE

VARIABLES
    holder,       \* player currently holding the token, or NONE if lost
    epoch,        \* the currently live token epoch
    owner,        \* epoch -> player minted to own that epoch (NONE if unminted)
    crashed,      \* set of players that have silently crashed
    committed,    \* history of committed actions: [player, epoch]
    beacon        \* lobby heartbeat lamp

vars == <<holder, epoch, owner, crashed, committed, beacon>>

Records == [player : Players, epoch : 1..MaxEpoch]

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Players \cup {NONE}
    /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
    /\ owner \in [1..MaxEpoch -> Players \cup {NONE}]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Players
    /\ committed \in Seq(Records)
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ \E p \in Players :
         /\ holder = p
         /\ owner = [e \in 1..MaxEpoch |-> IF e = 1 THEN p ELSE NONE]
    /\ epoch = 1
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ committed = << >>
    /\ beacon = FALSE

\* Hand the single exclusive token onward, minting a fresh higher epoch.
PassToken(nxt) ==
    /\ holder \in Players
    /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ nxt # holder
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ LET ne == epoch + 1
       IN /\ epoch' = ne
          /\ holder' = nxt
          /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![ne] = nxt]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, committed, beacon>>

\* A live player regenerates a lost token at a still-higher epoch.
Regen(m) ==
    /\ (holder = NONE \/ holder \in crashed)
    /\ m \notin crashed
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ LET ne == epoch + 1 IN
         /\ epoch' = ne
         /\ holder' = m
         /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![ne] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, committed, beacon>>

\* Only the current holder may commit, stamping its player and the live epoch.
Act(n) ==
    /\ holder = n
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ \A i \in DOMAIN committed : committed[i].epoch # epoch
    /\ committed' = Append(committed, [player |-> n, epoch |-> epoch])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, owner, crashed, beacon>>

Crash(n) ==
    /\ n \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, owner, committed, beacon>>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, owner, crashed, committed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Players : PassToken(m)
    \/ \E m \in Players : Regen(m)
    \/ \E n \in Players : Act(n)
    \/ \E n \in Players : Crash(n)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAction ==
    /\ \A i \in 1..Len(committed) :
         /\ committed[i].epoch <= epoch
         /\ owner[committed[i].epoch] = committed[i].player
    /\ \A i \in 1..(Len(committed) - 1) :
         committed[i].epoch <= committed[i + 1].epoch

=============================================================================

CONSTANTS
    Players = {n1, n2, n3}
    MaxEpoch = 3
    NONE = none

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT NoUnauthorizedOrStaleAction
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby uses a circulating token to decide which player is currently allowed to modify the shared lobby, for example to start the match. The players are arranged in a ring, and the token is handed from one player to the ring successor; every time the token moves it is minted with a fresh, strictly higher epoch number, and the mint records which player owns that epoch. Only the player holding the current token may commit a lobby action, and each committed action is stamped with the acting player and the epoch under which it acted. A player may crash silently at any moment, becoming unresponsive without telling anyone; if the token was in the hands of a crashed player it is effectively lost, and any live player may regenerate a brand-new token at a still-higher epoch to recover. The hazard is that a crashed-and-forgotten player, or a player replaying an old token, could commit a lobby action it is no longer entitled to. Every committed action must therefore trace back to the genuine owner of the epoch it claims, and must never claim an epoch newer than the one currently live, and epochs across the action history must never run backwards.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed lobby action was performed by the recorded owner of the epoch it is stamped with, that epoch never exceeds the currently live epoch, and the stamped epochs never decrease down the action history, so no unauthorized or stale player ever acts.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m7p0t0 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, FREE

VARIABLES
    reg,          \* compare-and-swap ownership register: a controller or FREE
    inCS,         \* controllers currently in the shedding critical section
    requesting,   \* controllers that have registered intent to shed
    crashed,      \* controllers that have silently crashed
    beacon        \* grid heartbeat

vars == <<reg, inCS, requesting, crashed, beacon>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in Controllers \cup {FREE}
    /\ inCS \subseteq Controllers
    /\ requesting \subseteq Controllers
    /\ crashed \subseteq Controllers
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ reg = FREE
    /\ inCS = {}
    /\ requesting = {}
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ beacon = FALSE

Request(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ c \notin requesting
    /\ c \notin inCS
    /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, inCS, crashed, beacon>>

\* compare-and-swap FREE -> c
Acquire(c) ==
    /\ c \in requesting
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ reg = FREE
    /\ reg' = c
    /\ inCS' = inCS \cup {c}
    /\ requesting' = requesting \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, beacon>>

\* compare-and-swap c -> FREE
Release(c) ==
    /\ c \in inCS
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ reg = c
    /\ reg' = FREE
    /\ inCS' = inCS \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<requesting, crashed, beacon>>

\* Silent crash: stops shedding but leaves the register jammed at c.
Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {c}
    /\ inCS' = inCS \ {c}
    /\ requesting' = requesting \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, beacon>>

\* Watchdog reclaims a jammed lock via compare-and-swap deadOwner -> FREE.
Watchdog(c) ==
    /\ c \in crashed
    /\ reg = c
    /\ reg' = FREE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, requesting, crashed, beacon>>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, inCS, requesting, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Request(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Acquire(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Release(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Crash(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Watchdog(c)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The register names whoever holds the critical section; two occupants
\* are impossible because a single register cannot name two controllers.
CriticalSectionMatchesRegister ==
    \A c \in inCS : reg = c

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {a, b, c}
    FREE = free

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT CriticalSectionMatchesRegister
nl:
A regional power grid runs an automated load-shedding scheme where several substation controllers may each want to shed load, but only one controller may be actively shedding at any instant, otherwise the grid would be over-shed and blacked out. Coordination goes through a single compare-and-swap ownership register that names the controller currently entitled to shed, or a special FREE marker. A controller first registers its intent to shed, then tries to acquire the register with a compare-and-swap that only succeeds when the register reads FREE, atomically writing its own identity. Having acquired, the controller enters the critical shedding section; when finished it compare-and-swaps the register from its own identity back to FREE. A controller can crash silently at any moment; if it crashes while shedding it stops acting but leaves the register still pointing at it, jamming the lock. A watchdog notices a crashed owner and compare-and-swaps the register from that dead owner back to FREE so progress can resume. The essential requirement is that the register faithfully names whoever is in the shedding section, which is what keeps two controllers from ever shedding at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every controller currently in the shedding critical section is exactly the controller named by the ownership register, so two controllers can never occupy the critical section at once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od1m8p5t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Flights, Runways, NONE

VARIABLES
    sector,       \* coarse lock: flight holding the airport sector, or NONE
    runway,       \* fine locks: runway -> flight holding it, or NONE
    takeoffLog,   \* append-only record of flights cleared for takeoff
    requests,     \* pending, reorderable clearance requests
    beacon

vars == <<sector, runway, takeoffLog, requests, beacon>>

ClearedSet == { takeoffLog[i] : i \in 1..Len(takeoffLog) }

TypeOK ==
    /\ sector \in Flights \cup {NONE}
    /\ runway \in [Runways -> Flights \cup {NONE}]
    /\ takeoffLog \in Seq(Flights)
    /\ requests \subseteq Flights
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ sector = NONE
    /\ runway = [r \in Runways |-> NONE]
    /\ takeoffLog = << >>
    /\ requests = {}
    /\ beacon = FALSE

RequestClearance(f) ==
    /\ f \notin requests
    /\ requests' = requests \cup {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, runway, takeoffLog, beacon>>

\* Coarse lock first: acquire the sector.
AcquireSector(f) ==
    /\ f \in requests
    /\ sector = NONE
    /\ sector' = f
    /\ UNCHANGED <<runway, takeoffLog, requests, beacon>>

\* Fine lock, only while holding the coarse sector lock.
AcquireRunway(f, r) ==
    /\ sector = f
    /\ runway[r] = NONE
    /\ runway' = [runway EXCEPT ![r] = f]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, takeoffLog, requests, beacon>>

\* Irreversible takeoff clearance; then release both locks.
Clear(f, r) ==
    /\ sector = f
    /\ runway[r] = f
    /\ f \notin ClearedSet
    /\ takeoffLog' = Append(takeoffLog, f)
    /\ runway' = [runway EXCEPT ![r] = NONE]
    /\ sector' = NONE
    /\ requests' = requests \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED beacon

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<sector, runway, takeoffLog, requests>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Flights : RequestClearance(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : AcquireSector(f)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : AcquireRunway(f, r)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, r \in Runways : Clear(f, r)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoRepeatTakeoff ==
    Cardinality(ClearedSet) = Len(takeoffLog)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Flights = {f1, f2}
    Runways = {r1, r2}
    NONE = none

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT NoRepeatTakeoff
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator clears flights for takeoff, which is an irreversible action once the flight rolls. To be cleared, a flight must first acquire a coarse lock on the whole airport sector and then, while holding the sector, acquire a fine lock on the specific runway it will use. Clearance requests from flights arrive over a data link that can reorder them, so the allocator may pick up a later request before an earlier one, and a re-submitted request for the same flight can also surface out of order. Once a flight holds both the sector lock and its runway lock, the tower issues the physical takeoff clearance, appending the flight to an append-only takeoff record and then releasing both the runway and the sector for others. Because requests can be reordered and resubmitted, a flight might momentarily appear eligible to be cleared a second time. The allocator keeps a single takeoff record, and the rule is that a flight never appears in it more than once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of distinct flights in the takeoff record always equals the record's length, so no flight is ever cleared for takeoff more than once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od3m2p6t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Banks, MaxEpoch

Votes == {"none", "yes", "no"}
Phases == {"init", "preparing", "committed", "aborted"}

VARIABLES
    phase,        \* coordinator phase for the current batch
    vote,         \* bank -> its vote in this round
    voteEpoch,    \* bank -> epoch its vote was cast under (0 = no vote)
    enrolled,     \* banks currently authorized to participate
    epoch,        \* current batch epoch
    beacon

vars == <<phase, vote, voteEpoch, enrolled, epoch, beacon>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in Phases
    /\ vote \in [Banks -> Votes]
    /\ voteEpoch \in [Banks -> 0..MaxEpoch]
    /\ enrolled \subseteq Banks
    /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ phase = "init"
    /\ vote = [b \in Banks |-> "none"]
    /\ voteEpoch = [b \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ enrolled = Banks
    /\ epoch = 1
    /\ beacon = FALSE

OpenBatch ==
    /\ phase = "init"
    /\ enrolled # {}
    /\ phase' = "preparing"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, voteEpoch, enrolled, epoch, beacon>>

CastVote(b, v) ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ b \in enrolled
    /\ vote[b] = "none"
    /\ v \in {"yes", "no"}
    /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![b] = v]
    /\ voteEpoch' = [voteEpoch EXCEPT ![b] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, enrolled, epoch, beacon>>

CommitBatch ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ \A b \in enrolled : vote[b] = "yes"
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, voteEpoch, enrolled, epoch, beacon>>

AbortBatch ==
    /\ phase = "preparing"
    /\ \E b \in enrolled : vote[b] = "no"
    /\ phase' = "aborted"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, voteEpoch, enrolled, epoch, beacon>>

\* Runtime capacity change: enroll/drop a bank, bump epoch, fresh round.
Reconfigure(b) ==
    /\ phase \in {"init", "committed", "aborted"}
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ enrolled' = IF b \in enrolled THEN enrolled \ {b} ELSE enrolled \cup {b}
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ phase' = "init"
    /\ vote' = [b2 \in Banks |-> "none"]
    /\ voteEpoch' = [b2 \in Banks |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED beacon

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, vote, voteEpoch, enrolled, epoch>>

Next ==
    \/ OpenBatch
    \/ \E b \in Banks, v \in {"yes", "no"} : CastVote(b, v)
    \/ CommitBatch
    \/ AbortBatch
    \/ \E b \in Banks : Reconfigure(b)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyEnrolledCurrentEpochVotes ==
    \A b \in Banks :
        (vote[b] # "none") => (b \in enrolled /\ voteEpoch[b] = epoch)

=============================================================================
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Banks = {b1, b2}
    MaxEpoch = 3

INIT Init
NEXT Next

INVARIANT OnlyEnrolledCurrentEpochVotes
nl:
A bank runs interbank settlement in batches, each coordinated by a two-phase commit protocol across the participating member banks. The coordinator opens a batch by moving into the preparing phase and asking every enrolled bank to vote. Each enrolled bank casts a single yes or no vote, and the vote is stamped with the batch epoch it was cast under. If all enrolled banks vote yes the batch commits; if any votes no it aborts. Crucially, the membership set can change at runtime: banks are enrolled or dropped between batches as settlement capacity is adjusted, and every such reconfiguration bumps the batch epoch and starts a fresh, empty round of voting. This means a vote left over from an earlier configuration is stale, and a bank that is not currently enrolled is unauthorized. The danger is that a stale vote from a prior epoch, or a vote from a non-member bank, gets counted toward the current settlement decision. The protocol must guarantee that any vote on record belongs to a currently enrolled bank and carries the current epoch.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every recorded vote comes from a currently enrolled bank and is stamped with the current batch epoch, so no unauthorized or stale participant ever contributes to a settlement.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m8p0t5 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Depts, CourseIds, Editors, Admin, NONE

Courses == Depts \X CourseIds
DeptOf(c) == c[1]

VARIABLES
    deptLock,     \* dept -> editor holding coarse lock, or NONE
    session,      \* course -> set of editors inside its edit session
    pending,      \* filed edit requests: set of <<editor, course>>
    beacon

vars == <<deptLock, session, pending, beacon>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ deptLock \in [Depts -> Editors \cup {NONE}]
    /\ session \in [Courses -> SUBSET Editors]
    /\ pending \subseteq (Editors \X Courses)
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ deptLock = [d \in Depts |-> NONE]
    /\ session = [c \in Courses |-> {}]
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ beacon = FALSE

Request(e, c) ==
    /\ <<e, c>> \notin pending
    /\ session[c] = {}
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<e, c>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, session, beacon>>

AcquireDept(e, d) ==
    /\ deptLock[d] = NONE
    /\ \E c \in Courses : (DeptOf(c) = d /\ <<e, c>> \in pending)
    /\ deptLock' = [deptLock EXCEPT ![d] = e]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, pending, beacon>>

EnterEdit(e, c) ==
    /\ <<e, c>> \in pending
    /\ e = deptLock[DeptOf(c)]
    /\ session[c] = {}
    /\ session' = [session EXCEPT ![c] = {e}]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {<<e, c>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, beacon>>

LeaveEdit(e, c) ==
    /\ e \in session[c]
    /\ session' = [session EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, pending, beacon>>

ReleaseDept(e, d) ==
    /\ deptLock[d] = e
    /\ \A c \in Courses : (DeptOf(c) = d) => (session[c] = {})
    /\ deptLock' = [deptLock EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<session, pending, beacon>>

\* Privileged admin override: seize a course's session and both locks atomically.
AdminOverride(c) ==
    /\ deptLock' = [deptLock EXCEPT ![DeptOf(c)] = Admin]
    /\ session' = [session EXCEPT ![c] = {Admin}]
    /\ pending' = pending \ {<<e, c>> : e \in Editors}
    /\ UNCHANGED beacon

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<deptLock, session, pending>>

Next ==
    \/ \E e \in Editors, c \in Courses : Request(e, c)
    \/ \E e \in Editors, d \in Depts : AcquireDept(e, d)
    \/ \E e \in Editors, c \in Courses : EnterEdit(e, c)
    \/ \E e \in Editors, c \in Courses : LeaveEdit(e, c)
    \/ \E e \in Editors, d \in Depts : ReleaseDept(e, d)
    \/ \E c \in Courses : AdminOverride(c)
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EditorHoldsDeptLock ==
    \A c \in Courses :
        \A e \in session[c] : deptLock[DeptOf(c)] = e

=============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system lets registrars edit the seat tables of individual courses, but a course's seat table is a critical resource that only one editor may hold at a time. Editing uses hierarchical locks: an editor must first take the coarse lock on the course's department, and only while holding that department lock may it enter the fine-grained edit session for a specific course in that department. A registrar first files a request to edit a course; later it acquires the department lock, then opens the edit session, then closes the session and releases the department. Because the department lock is single-holder, at most one registrar can be editing any course in that department, which is what enforces exclusive access. There is also a privileged administrator who can override the locks: the admin may seize a course's edit session directly, evicting whoever holds it and taking both the department lock and the edit session in one atomic step. The system must guarantee that whoever is inside a course's edit session is precisely the holder of that course's department lock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Any editor inside a course's edit session must be the current holder of that course's department lock, so two different editors can never be editing the same course at once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m5p6t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Validators, Instances, PropIds, Quorum, MaxVer

Proposals == Instances \X PropIds

VARIABLES
    memberVer,    \* validator -> config version it was admitted at (0 = never)
    configVer,    \* current roster configuration version
    votes,        \* proposal -> set of validators that voted for it
    executed,     \* proposals that reached quorum and ran
    beacon

vars == <<memberVer, configVer, votes, executed, beacon>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ memberVer \in [Validators -> 0..MaxVer]
    /\ configVer \in 1..MaxVer
    /\ votes \in [Proposals -> SUBSET Validators]
    /\ executed \subseteq Proposals
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ memberVer = [v \in Validators |-> 0]
    /\ configVer = 1
    /\ votes = [p \in Proposals |-> {}]
    /\ executed = {}
    /\ beacon = FALSE

\* Admit (or re-admit a stale) validator at the current version.
Admit(v) ==
    /\ memberVer[v] # configVer
    /\ memberVer' = [memberVer EXCEPT ![v] = configVer]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<configVer, votes, executed, beacon>>

CastVote(v, p) ==
    /\ memberVer[v] = configVer
    /\ v \notin votes[p]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = @ \cup {v}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<memberVer, configVer, executed, beacon>>

Execute(p) ==
    /\ Cardinality(votes[p]) >= Quorum
    /\ p \notin executed
    /\ executed' = executed \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<memberVer, configVer, votes, beacon>>

\* Roster reconfiguration: bump version, clear the shared vote pool.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ configVer < MaxVer
    /\ configVer' = configVer + 1
    /\ votes' = [p \in Proposals |-> {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<memberVer, executed, beacon>>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<memberVer, configVer, votes, executed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E v \in Validators : Admit(v)
    \/ \E v \in Validators, p \in Proposals : CastVote(v, p)
    \/ \E p \in Proposals : Execute(p)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ Heartbeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AllCountedVotesCurrent ==
    \A p \in Proposals :
        \A v \in votes[p] : memberVer[v] = configVer

=============================================================================
nl:

    term,         \* election term
    alive,        \* set of nodes still alive
    slotBag,      \* slot -> bag occupying it, or NONE (forward binding)
    bagSlot,      \* bag -> slot it holds, or NONE (reverse binding)
    beacon

vars == <<leader, term, alive, slotBag, bagSlot, beacon>>

    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {NONE}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ alive \subseteq Nodes
    /\ slotBag \in [Slots -> Bags \cup {NONE}]
    /\ bagSlot \in [Bags -> Slots \cup {NONE}]
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term = 0
    /\ alive = Nodes
    /\ slotBag = [s \in Slots |-> NONE]
    /\ bagSlot = [b \in Bags |-> NONE]
    /\ beacon = FALSE

Fail(n) ==
    /\ n \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {n}
    /\ leader' = IF leader = n THEN NONE ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, slotBag, bagSlot, beacon>>

Elect(n) ==
    /\ n \in alive
    /\ leader = NONE
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alive, slotBag, bagSlot, beacon>>

Allocate(n, b, s) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ n \in alive
    /\ slotBag[s] = NONE
    /\ bagSlot[b] = NONE
    /\ slotBag' = [slotBag EXCEPT ![s] = b]
    /\ bagSlot' = [bagSlot EXCEPT ![b] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, beacon>>

\* Privileged admin override: detach prior bindings, then rebind consistently.
AdminOverride(b, s) ==
    /\ LET oldBag == slotBag[s]
           oldSlot == bagSlot[b]
       IN /\ slotBag' = [t \in Slots |->
                            IF t = s THEN b
                            ELSE IF t = oldSlot THEN NONE
                            ELSE slotBag[t]]
          /\ bagSlot' = [c \in Bags |->
                            IF c = b THEN s
                            ELSE IF c = oldBag THEN NONE
                            ELSE bagSlot[c]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, beacon>>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, alive, slotBag, bagSlot>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Fail(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, b \in Bags, s \in Slots : Allocate(n, b, s)
    \/ \E b \in Bags, s \in Slots : AdminOverride(b, s)
    \/ Heartbeat

    \A b \in Bags : (bagSlot[b] # NONE) => (slotBag[bagSlot[b]] = b)

An airport baggage router assigns bags to chute slots. Each allocation binds a bag to a slot and simultaneously records the reverse binding from the bag back to the slot, so the two directions must always agree. A slot may only be allocated when it is free and the bag being placed does not already hold a slot. The safety concern is double allocation: a stale or split-brain leader trying to hand the same slot to a second bag while the first bag still believes it owns that slot. The invariant the router must preserve is that whenever a bag records that it holds a slot, that slot records the very same bag as its occupant.

    /\ cap \in [Cars -> 0..MaxCap]
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ reserved \subseteq (Instances \X Cars)

    /\ cap = [c \in Cars |-> MaxCap]
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ reserved = {}
    /\ beacon = FALSE

Reserve(i, c) ==
    /\ <<i, c>> \notin reserved
    /\ load[c] < cap[c]
    /\ reserved' = reserved \cup {<<i, c>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, cap, epoch, beacon>>

\* Boarding is admitted only if there is still room -- the true capacity guard.
Board(i, c) ==
    /\ <<i, c>> \in reserved
    /\ load[c] < cap[c]
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![c] = @ + 1]
    /\ reserved' = reserved \ {<<i, c>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, epoch, beacon>>

Alight(c) ==
    /\ load[c] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![c] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, epoch, reserved, beacon>>

Transfer(c1, c2) ==
    /\ c1 # c2
    /\ load[c1] > 0
    /\ load[c2] < cap[c2]
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![c1] = @ - 1, ![c2] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, epoch, reserved, beacon>>

\* Epoch-numbered reconfiguration; capacity must not drop below current load.
Reconfigure(c, newcap) ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ newcap >= load[c]
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![c] = newcap]
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, reserved, beacon>>

Heartbeat ==
    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, cap, epoch, reserved>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, c \in Cars : Reserve(i, c)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, c \in Cars : Board(i, c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Alight(c)
    \/ \E c1 \in Cars, c2 \in Cars : Transfer(c1, c2)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, newcap \in 0..MaxCap : Reconfigure(c, newcap)
    \/ Heartbeat

    applied,      \* record -> sequence of base versions of applied updates

    /\ applied = [r \in Records |-> << >>]

\* Read the current version and submit an update stamped with it.
Submit(w, r) ==
    /\ <<w, r, version[r]>> \notin inflight
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {<<w, r, version[r]>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, applied, beacon>>

Apply(w, r, bv) ==

    /\ bv = version[r]
    /\ version[r] < MaxVer
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ applied' = [applied EXCEPT ![r] = Append(@, bv)]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {<<w, r, bv>>}

    /\ bv # version[r]
    /\ inflight' = inflight \ {<<w, r, bv>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, applied, beacon>>

    \/ \E w \in Workers, r \in Records, bv \in 0..MaxVer : Reject(w, r, bv)

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps a versioned record for each blood product. Workers use optimistic concurrency: a worker reads a record together with its current version number and later submits an update stamped with the version it read. Because submissions travel over a bus that can reorder them, an update may be delivered out of order, well after other updates have already advanced the record. When an update is delivered, it is applied only if the version it was stamped with still matches the record's current version; applying an update advances the version by one. If the stamped version no longer matches, the update is stale and is rejected, and the worker must retry by re-reading the fresh version and submitting again. The hazard is that a reordered, stale update from a worker acting on an out-of-date view gets applied, corrupting the count. The tracker keeps, for each record, the list of base versions of the updates it actually applied. The correctness requirement is that this list is always exactly the consecutive versions the record passed through, with no gap and no repeat.
SAFETY PROPERTY: For every record, the applied updates' stamped base versions are exactly the consecutive numbers zero, one, two and so on up to the current version, so no stale or out-of-order update is ever applied.

    gen,          \* segment -> generation counter
    routedBy,     \* segment -> instance currently routing, or NONE
    routedGen,    \* segment -> generation the active router acquired under

    /\ owner \in [Segments -> Instances \cup {FREE}]
    /\ gen \in [Segments -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ routedBy \in [Segments -> Instances \cup {NONE}]
    /\ routedGen \in [Segments -> 0..MaxGen]
    /\ beacon \in BOOLEAN

    /\ gen = [s \in Segments |-> 0]
    /\ routedBy = [s \in Segments |-> NONE]
    /\ routedGen = [s \in Segments |-> 0]
    /\ beacon = FALSE

Acquire(i, s) ==
    /\ owner[s] = FREE
    /\ gen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routedBy, routedGen, beacon>>

\* CAS other -> i, bumping generation and invalidating the old owner's routing.
Preempt(i, s) ==

    /\ owner[s] # i
    /\ gen[s] < MaxGen
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ gen' = [gen EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ routedBy' = [routedBy EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<routedGen, beacon>>

    /\ routedBy' = [routedBy EXCEPT ![s] = i]
    /\ routedGen' = [routedGen EXCEPT ![s] = gen[s]]

    /\ routedBy' = [routedBy EXCEPT ![s] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, gen, routedGen, beacon>>

    /\ owner[s] = i
    /\ routedBy[s] # i
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = FREE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gen, routedBy, routedGen, beacon>>

    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, gen, routedBy, routedGen>>

Writes == [baseVer : 0..MaxVer, content : SUBSET Contribs, contrib : Contribs]

    /\ recContent = {}
    /\ committed = {}
    /\ prepared = [c \in Controllers |-> NONE]

ReadModify(c, x) ==

                       contrib |-> x]]

    /\ recVersion < MaxVer
    /\ recContent' = prepared[c].content
    /\ recVersion' = recVersion + 1
    /\ committed' = committed \cup {prepared[c].contrib}
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![c] = NONE]

    /\ prepared[c].baseVer # recVersion

    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Reject(c)
    \/ Heartbeat

NoLostUpdates ==

A skyscraper elevator bank keeps a single shared assignment record that several controllers update using optimistic concurrency. To make a change, a controller reads the record together with its version, computes a new content that adds its own contribution to the snapshot it read, and later writes the whole new content back. The write is accepted only if the record's version still matches the version the controller originally read; if it matches, the record is replaced with the computed content and the version advances by one. A controller can be slow but never fails: its prepared write may sit outstanding for a long time while other controllers race ahead and commit their own changes, but it will eventually either commit or be found stale. A stale write, computed from an out-of-date snapshot, is rejected and the controller must retry. The danger is a lost update: a slow write built on an old snapshot overwrites the record and silently drops the contributions that were committed in the meantime. The system tracks the set of all contributions that have ever been successfully committed, and requires the live record to contain exactly that set.

An operator prepares an update by reading the manifest's current total together with its version, and computes a new total by adding the number of containers it just moved. Later it commits, writing the whole new total back, but the commit is accepted only if the manifest's version still matches the version the operator read; a successful commit advances the version and adds the operator's contribution to the running tally of everything ever committed. The yard requires the manifest's total to always equal the tally of all container contributions ever committed.

    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = shelfVersion]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, inTransit, dispensed, shelfVersion, beacon>>

\* Optimistic reserve; serviced out of order, applied only if version still matches.
Reserve(w) ==
    /\ pending[w] # NONE
    /\ pending[w] = shelfVersion
    /\ stock > 0
    /\ shelfVersion < MaxVer
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit + 1
    /\ shelfVersion' = shelfVersion + 1
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<dispensed, beacon>>

RejectStale(w) ==
    /\ pending[w] # NONE
    /\ pending[w] # shelfVersion
    /\ pending' = [pending EXCEPT ![w] = NONE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, inTransit, dispensed, shelfVersion, beacon>>

    /\ inTransit' = inTransit - 1
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, shelfVersion, pending, beacon>>

    /\ dispensed > 0
    /\ shelfVersion < MaxVer
    /\ dispensed' = dispensed - 1
    /\ stock' = stock + 1
    /\ shelfVersion' = shelfVersion + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inTransit, pending, beacon>>

    /\ beacon' = ~beacon
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, inTransit, dispensed, shelfVersion, pending>>

    \/ \E w \in Workers : Reserve(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : RejectStale(w)
    \/ Deliver
    \/ Return
    \/ Heartbeat

A pharmacy prescription dispenser manages a fixed quantity of pills that must be conserved: every pill is always either on the shelf as stock, in transit through processing, or already dispensed, and pills are never created or destroyed. Workers move pills using optimistic concurrency on the shelf stock. A worker files a request stamped with the shelf's current version, and because requests travel over a bus that can reorder them, either worker's request may be serviced before the other's. Reserving a pill succeeds only if the version stamped on the request still matches the shelf version; a successful reserve moves one pill from stock into transit and advances the shelf version. If the version has moved on, the request is stale and is rejected so the worker can retry from a fresh read. A pill in transit is later delivered, moving it from transit into the dispensed count, and a dispensed pill can be returned to the shelf, moving it back into stock. Throughout all of this the total number of pills across the shelf, transit, and dispensed buckets must stay exactly constant.

A smart-home door lock network keeps one shared access-policy record replicated across the lock nodes, and changes to it are applied through a two-phase commit. A coordinator opens a transaction by proposing a policy entry to add, which moves the protocol into the voting phase and clears the previous round's votes. Each participant lock acknowledges by voting yes, but these acknowledgements travel over the home network and can be reordered, so one lock's vote may be delivered before another's regardless of order sent. Only when every participant has voted yes does the coordinator commit, atomically adding the proposed entry both to the live shared record and to the durable set of everything ever committed, and moving into the committed phase. If a round cannot gather all votes it may be aborted, which changes nothing and returns to idle, and after a commit the protocol resets to idle for the next change. The concern is lost updates: a committed policy change that fails to land in the shared record, whether due to reordered messages or a botched commit. The network requires the live shared record to always equal exactly the set of policy entries ever committed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The live shared access-policy record always equals the set of all policy entries ever committed, so no committed update is ever lost.
